sec.title: Background
sec.p: Glioma, a tumor derived from neuroglial cells of the central nervous system, is characterized by its high malignancy, frequent recurrence, and high mortality rate. Recent advances in exosome research related to gliomas have propelled this emerging field as a pivotal area of clinical neuroscience investigation. Despite extensive focus on glioma exosome research, a systematic visual analysis of this field remains lacking. Using bibliometric analysis, this study maps the scientific landscape of glioma exosome research to identify current hotspots and emerging trends in neuro-oncology.

sec.title: Methods
sec.p: This bibliometric analysis extracted glioma exosome publications from the Web of Science Core Collection(WoSCC) spanning 2005–2025. Following systematic screening, 209 articles constituted the analytic corpus. Using VOSviewer(VOS), Scimago Graphica, and CiteSpace, we mapped contributions across geographic, institutional, authorship, and conceptual domains. This visualization delineates the field’s intellectual structure, identifies current research foci, and projects emerging trends in neuro-oncology.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: Annual publication volume on glioma exosomes has increased significantly since 2019. China and the United States are the predominant contributors, collectively driving field advancement. Leading institutions include Shandong University, Shandong Provincial Key Laboratory of Brain Function Reconstruction, and Capital Medical University, whose productivity metrics reflect substantial influence. Notably, Chinese institutions comprise 90% of the top 10 productive entities. Key investigators Li Gang and Xue Hao demonstrate exceptional scholarly output, advancing the field through high-impact research. NEURO-ONCOLOGY emerges as the premier journal, evidenced by its dominant citation frequency. Thematic analysis reveals three conceptual domains: Exosome biogenesis in gliomas, Glioblastoma extracellular vesicle signatures, and Exosome mediated drug delivery systems-representing current priorities and evolving research frontiers.

sec.title: Conclusion
sec.p: Exosomes have attracted considerable attention in glioma research, establishing themselves as a cutting edge thematic focus. This study applies bibliometric rigor to map research trajectories and conceptual evolution in glioma exosomes. The analysis establishes foundational frameworks that prioritize future investigation domains while objectively quantifying the field’s translational potential. These evidence-based insights will accelerate mechanistic discovery and clinical translation in neuro-oncology.
Keywords: Exosome, Glioma, Drug delivery, Bibliometric analysis

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Gliomas represent the most prevalent malignant primary the central nervous system (CNS) tumors, constituting 80% of such malignancies per Central Brain Tumor Registry of the United States data [1]. Gliomas, the most prevalent malignant primary CNS tumors, exhibit aggressive behavior and therapeutic recalcitrance. Per the World Health Organization classification, they stratify into four histological grades: grades I-II (low-grade) and III-IV (high-grade). High-grade variants portend particularly poor prognoses, with median survival under 15 months. Even low-grade gliomas demonstrate limited long-term control, showing only 39% 10-year survival rates. These features-frequent recurrence, disabling morbidity, and refractory mortality collectively establish gliomas as persistently intractable clinical challenges [2]. In glioma treatment, three core therapeutic modalities currently form the cornerstone of comprehensive management. First, surgical intervention is the primary approach, aiming to achieve maximal tumor resection to directly reduce the tumor burden. Second, radiotherapy acts as a critical adjuvant, utilizing precise external irradiation to target residual tumor cells. Finally, chemotherapy, administered systemically or locally, targets tumor cells pharmacologically, thereby consolidating the effects of surgery and radiotherapy and preventing recurrence. These three modalities complement each other and form an essential component of glioma management [3]. Despite the critical role of current mainstream treatments, including surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, in the management of gliomas, these approaches have not significantly reduced disease recurrence. Clinically, therapeutic options for gliomas remain limited and face numerous challenges. Notably, the blood-brain barrier (BBB), a key physiological structure, significantly impedes drug penetration into brain tissue. Additionally, the high drug resistance of glioma cells further diminishes treatment efficacy. For example, although drugs such as temozolomide, bevacizumab, cetuximab, and lomustine have been widely used in glioma treatment for decades, their efficacy remains limited. These challenges highlight the urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies, particularly those capable of overcoming the BBB and addressing glioma drug resistance. Therefore, exploring glioma specific treatment pathways and developing novel drugs that can penetrate the BBB and reverse drug resistance are now top priorities in glioma research [4]. The development of innovative therapeutic strategies for glioma is therefore critically important. Several emerging therapies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors and chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapies, have shown promise in clinical trials. However, these advancements have thus far not yielded the desired outcomes in glioma management. Consequently, while these novel approaches hold potential, further research and optimization are essential before they can be routinely implemented in clinical practice [5]. Exosomes, as a novel therapeutic strategy, have shown significant potential and promising applications in glioma treatment.

Exosomes are endosome-derived small extracellular vesicles (40–150 nm in diameter) secreted by a variety of cell types. They have quickly become a major research focus over the past decade [6]. Their biogenesis initiates with plasma membrane invagination, and their secretion levels and molecular cargo are regulated by specific biogenesis mechanisms, cellular origin, and physiological state. Critically, exosomes function as key mediators of intercellular communication. By transporting diverse bioactive molecules-including proteins, nucleic acids, and lipids-they exert significant regulatory influence on tumor initiation and progression [7]. Exosomes have gained significant traction in glioma research, particularly for prognosis and therapeutic development. Recent studies reveal that exosome mediated transfer of tumor suppressor miR-3591-3p promotes M2-type macrophage polarization, accelerating glioma progression. These discoveries not only provide novel molecular insights into the role of exosomes in glioma development but also offer forward-looking perspectives for innovating glioma treatment strategies [8]. Exosomes demonstrate significant clinical utility as biomarkers in glioblastoma (GBM) research. Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction analysis reveals markedly elevated exosomal miR-210 levels in GBM patient serum versus healthy controls. Critically, Kaplan-Meier analysis establishes exosomal miR-210 (exo-miR-210) as both a diagnostic biomarker and independent prognostic indicator, with additional utility for assessing tumor hypoxia. These findings underscore the translational value of exosomal biomarkers in GBM clinical management pathways [9]. Recently, exosomes have gained significant attention as an emerging therapeutic strategy for glioma. Research has shown that exosomal microRNAs (miRNAs) can modulate multiple signaling pathways, closely linking them to glioma pathogenesis. These findings not only provide a strong scientific basis for exosome based glioma therapy but also reveal their potential to modulate tumor biology, opening new avenues for glioma treatment research [10]. Exosomal miRNAs critically regulate drug resistance in GBM through precise targeting of signaling pathways and direct modulation of key proteins/genes [11]. Exosomes have provided a multifaceted perspective for analyzing the pathogenesis of gliomas and other tumors, opening new avenues for therapeutic strategies and drug development. With their unique ability to cross the BBB, nanoscale size, and precise targeting, exosomes exhibit remarkable biological properties. As extracellular vesicles, exosomes inherently possess multifunctional carrier potential and are emerging as therapeutic tools. Extensive research has demonstrated that exosomes can serve as innovative drug delivery vehicles, playing a significant role in treating various diseases. These findings highlight the potential of exosomes in drug delivery systems and emphasize their broad applications in treating diseases that are challenging for traditional drugs, particularly brain tumors.

Bibliometrics applies quantitative methods to analyze scholarly publications, employing statistical tools to identify publication trends and map knowledge networks within academic literature. This approach systematically quantifies bibliographic elements-including publication volume, type, authorship distribution, and citation patterns-to reveal research domain evolution and structural relationships [12]. The application of bibliometrics in medicine is experiencing robust growth. This trend signifies an important frontier in the advancement of bibliometric knowledge [13]. However, the application of bibliometrics in glioma and exosome research remains limited. Therefore, this study aims to use bibliometric methods to systematically map the knowledge structure of glioma exosome research and analyze its cutting edge trends and core research topics. This approach aims to Establish a conceptual framework for future research prioritization and domain advancement and to guide the further development of knowledge in this field.

sec.title: Data sources and search strategy
sec.p: The WoSCC, globally recognized as an authoritative citation database, includes over 18, 000 journals across 256 disciplines. In bibliometric analysis, the Science Citation Index Expanded (SCI-EXPANDED), part of the WoSCC by Thomson Reuters, is widely considered the most reliable data source. Compared to other databases, the WoSCC is highly regarded for its accurate categorization of document types.

On March 10, 2025, this study performed a systematic search on the WoS platform to comprehensively collect research literature on gliomas and exosomes published between 2005 and 2025. The search spanned multiple databases, including the SCI-EXPANDED, Current Chemical Reactions, and Index Chemicus. To ensure data accuracy and consistency and to minimize potential biases caused by daily updates to the WoSCC, all search activities were completed within one day.

The search formula we used was: ((((TS=(Glioma*)) OR TS=(“Glial Cell Tumor*”)) OR TS=(“Tumor*, Glial Cell”) OR TS=(“Mixed Glioma*”) OR TS=(“Glioma*, Mixed”) OR TS=(“Malignant Glioma”) OR TS=(“Glioma*, Malignant”) OR TS=(“Malignant Gliomas”)) AND ((TS =(“exosome*”)) OR TS=(“exosomal”))). After a literature search, 209 relevant articles were selected and identified (Fig. 1).

To ensure focus and linguistic consistency, we applied strict inclusion criteria, limiting the literature to research articles and review papers published in English. Following this screening, 658 articles met the inclusion criteria. To further refine the dataset, we carefully evaluated the titles and abstracts of each article to assess their relevance to the research theme of glioma and exosomes. For articles whose relevance was unclear based on titles and abstracts alone, we also examined the keywords within the articles and the keyword lists provided by the authors. When necessary, the full text was reviewed for a more comprehensive assessment. Through this rigorous screening process, we identified 209 highly relevant and reliable articles aligned with our research theme. This selection provides a solid foundation for subsequent analysis.

sec.title: Data analysis and visualization
sec.p: In this study, we utilized two advanced software tools, VOS and CiteSpace, to perform in depth data analysis and visualization of the rigorously screened literature. In the network maps generated by VOS, each node represents a distinct research entity, including countries, researchers, keywords, journals, and research institutions. The size of the nodes corresponds to their frequency of occurrence, while colors are used to distinguish different research clusters or time periods. The thickness of the connecting lines indicates the strength of associations, with thicker lines representing stronger connections between entities. Additionally, the density of the lines reflects the degree of interconnection among entities, with higher density indicating stronger correlations.

To comprehensively analyze the bibliometric data, we employed CiteSpace for multidimensional visualization. Specifically, we analyzed the collaboration network structure, the temporal evolution of keywords, keyword burst detection, and annual publication trends. These methods not only facilitated a macro level understanding of the research field’s dynamics but also provided micro level insights into collaboration patterns and detailed trends. Through these rigorous and systematic analyses, we gained a deeper understanding of the current status and development trends in glioma and exosome research.

sec.title: Annual publication output and trends
sec.p: The number of publications and publication trends are key indicators for evaluating the development status, research hotspots, and academic value of a field. They provide valuable insights into research activity and the level of academic interest in this field. Figure 2 comprehensively depicts the changes in publication numbers and development trends in glioma exosome research globally from January 2005 to March 2025. This research field began to emerge in 2011, with the number of related publications increasing from one in that year to 13 in 2024 (data for 2025 are current up to March). Within this period, 2022 marked the peak year of research output, with 40 publications. Despite slight declines in some years, the overall publication volume in this field has shown a steady upward trend. This growth reflects both the continuous expansion of glioma exosome research and the increasing attention and importance accorded to this field by the academic community.

sec.title: Author contributions and Co-cited authors
sec.p: This study included a total of 1,503 authors. Based on publication count and citation frequency, we identified the top ten most contributing authors (Table 1). Specifically, Li Gang and Xue Hao, each with 10 publications, were ranked as the most prolific authors. They were followed by Qiu Wei and Wang Shaobo, each with 9 publications.

To explore author collaboration patterns in depth, we performed a visual analysis using VOS (Fig. 3). The results revealed frequent collaborations among multiple authors, particularly Li, Gang and Xue, Hao; Qiu, Wei and Wang, Shaobo, who formed a tightly-knit research network and co-authored numerous publications. Among the top ten most published authors, Li Boyan and Pan Ziwei also exhibited similar close collaboration patterns. In terms of average citations per paper, xu, jianye ranked first with 114 citations, closely followed by Chen Zihang with 96.5 citations. Further analysis of the co-citation author network (Fig. 4) showed that Skog, J, Stupp, R and Théry, C, were the three most cited authors, followed by Guo, X.F. and Ostrom, Q.T. By analyzing this network, we further found that these highly cited authors maintained close collaborations, collectively forming the core research group in this field.

sec.title: Contributions of countries or regions
sec.p: Over the past two decades, 28 countries and regions have actively contributed to glioma exosome research (Fig. 5). Ranked by publication count, China leads with 141 publications, followed by the United States (n = 38), Italy and Iran (n = 13)(Table 2). The Vos map visually illustrates the extent of international research collaboration, with line thickness indicating the intensity of cooperation. Notably, the collaboration between China and the United States is prominently featured on the map, underscoring their strong partnership in this research field (Fig. 6). Further analysis shows that while China leads in publication count, Sweden has the highest average citation rate, with 227.5 citations per paper. United states follows closely with 108.8108 citations per paper, reflecting the significant impact of its research. The Norway ranks third with an average of 98.8 citations per paper (Table 2). Despite Sweden’s relatively low publication count, its high citation rate underscores its key role and contributions in glioma exosome research.

sec.title: Institutional contributions
sec.p: Based on articles and reviews indexed in the WoS, 380 institutions have contributed to glioma exosome research. Ranked by publication count, the leading institutions include Shandong University (n = 14), Shandong Key Laboratory of Brain Function Remodeling (n = 9), Capital Medical University (n = 8), Huazhong university science & technology (n = 8), Nanchang University (n = 7) (Table 3). Notably, among the top 10 institutions by number of publications, all but Shahid Beheshti Medical University in Iran (ranked 7th) are from China. This distribution highlights China’s absolute dominance in this field.

sec.title: Keywords
sec.p: Keywords encapsulate the core content of academic papers, and their analysis is crucial for tracking scientific progress. In-depth keyword analysis can effectively reveal research hotspots in a specific field. To identify research hotspots in glioma exosome research, we performed a keyword co-occurrence analysis on 209 selected articles (Fig. 9). A total of 957 keywords were identified during this analysis. Using VOS, the number of nodes reflects keyword diversity, while node size corresponds to keyword frequency. Connecting lines illustrate keyword associations; the number of lines indicates connection frequency, and line thickness reflects relationship strength. Among these keywords, ‘glioma’ (n = 91) was the most frequent, followed by ‘glioblastoma’ (n = 85), ‘exosome’ (n = 76), and ‘extracellular vesicle’ (n = 62). These high-frequency keywords represent the main research directions in glioma exosome research (Table 6).

Figure 10 illustrates the evolving research hotspots in glioma exosome research over time. From 2011 to 2017, dendritic cells were the focus of research. From 2016 to 2019, brain tumors received a great deal of attention, while GBM also received attention during 2016–2017. Recently, from 2021 to 2023, themes such as pathway, resistance, delivery and stem cell have gained increasing attention and are expected to shape current and future research directions. From 2011 to 2024, delivery had the highest burst strength (3.78), followed by pathway (2.87) and dendritic cells (2.59). Notably, since 2021, researchers have increasingly focused on therapy-related areas, as reflected by the frequent occurrence of keywords such as ‘pathway’ and ‘delivery’ in the literature. The high frequency of these terms underscores the growing importance of exosomes in glioma treatment research, potentially signaling new trends and future research directions.

sec.title: General information
sec.p: This study performed a comprehensive analysis of 209 documents indexed in the WoSCC from 2005 to 2025. Notably, glioma exosome research began to yield significant academic output in 2011, marking its emergence as a rapidly developing field. Over time, the number of annual publications and the total number of publications have been steadily increasing. This reflects the rapid development of glioma exosome research. Researchers have made significant progress in key areas such as exosomes, GBM, and extracellular vesicles, laying a solid foundation for further development in the field.

In terms of publication volume in glioma exosome research, China, the United States, and Iran rank as the top three countries. China leads with 141 publications, accounting for 67.46% of the total, reflecting its high research activity and strong capabilities in this field. In contrast, Sweden, with only 4 publications, has a total of 910 citations, averaging 227.5 citations per paper, giving it the highest average citation rate. This indicates that despite Sweden’s low publication output, its research has a significant academic impact, underscoring its important role in glioma exosome research.

In terms of publication volume in glioma exosome research, Shandong University, the Shandong Key Laboratory of Brain Function Reconstruction, and Capital medical university rank at the forefront. Notably, all top ten institutions by publication volume are from China. This reflects the strong emphasis Chinese research institutions have placed on glioma exosome research, with continuous investment of resources and active research efforts. This output dominance underscores China’s significant contribution to the global glioma exosome research landscape.

Scientifically productive US-China collaborations generate the highest research output in glioma exosome research, highlighting the critical importance of international partnerships. Such cooperation facilitates cross-border knowledge exchange and enables multidimensional approaches to key challenges through integrated expertise. These collaborative frameworks accelerate scientific progress while establishing transferable models for global research advancement.

Scholars Gang Li, Hao Xue, Wei Qiu, and Shaobo Wang have made substantial research contributions to glioma exosome studies, evidenced by high-impact publications and influential discoveries. Their work demonstrates significant field leadership through consistent scientific advancement and conceptual innovation in this domain.

Researchers in glioma exosome studies should prioritize high impact journals with substantial publication volumes and citation metrics. Key outlets include: CELL DEATH & DISEASE, INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MOLRCULAR SCIENCES, CANCER LETTERS, JOURNAL OF NEURO-ONCOLOGY, and CANCER CELL INTERNATIONAL. These journals consistently advance the field through significant research output, accelerate knowledge dissemination, and provide critical insights into emerging developments. By studying these journals, researchers can gain a comprehensive understanding of the latest developments and key issues, providing a strong theoretical foundation and cutting-edge insights for their research.

Keyword frequency analysis is a pivotal tool for delineating research hotspots and emerging trends in glioma exosome research. This approach offers explicit guidance to researchers, directly informing future advancements in targeted areas of inquiry. Core terms such as “exosome,” “glioma,” “glioblastoma,” and “extracellular vesicle” dominate the literature. Furthermore, keywords like “endothelial cell” and “pathway” are increasingly prevalent. Notably, terms such as “resistance,” “stem cell,” and “delivery” have exhibited a significant increase in usage frequency in recent years. This evolving keyword landscape not only reflects the current research focus and trajectory but also profoundly influences the field’s development. The rapid growth of these specific terms highlights contemporary research hotspots, enabling researchers to better grasp the field’s current dynamics. This enhanced understanding facilitates more accurate assessments of the value and feasibility of potential future research directions, thereby providing a robust foundation for scientific research planning and implementation.

sec.title: Research trends and hotspots
sec.p: Through keyword frequency and citation burst analysis, two predominant research domains in glioma exosome studies were identified. First, exosomes are being investigated as potential biomarkers to facilitate early glioma diagnosis and disease monitoring. Second, therapeutic strategies leveraging exosomes for glioma treatment are garnering increasing interest, with the goal of developing more effective targeted therapies. These findings delineate key scientific challenges while highlighting translational opportunities, thereby establishing a robust foundation for advancing and clinically translating glioma exosome research.

sec.title: The application of exosomes as potential biomarkers in glioma
sec.p: Biomarkers, defined as biochemical indicators reflecting structural or functional alterations in biological systems-ranging from organs to subcellular components play a critical role in disease diagnosis and staging. Within glioma derived exosomes, several promising biomarkers have been identified, including mutant IDH1, EGFRvIII, tumor-specific mRNA, various miRNAs, and notably miRNA-21. These biomarkers provide a substantial molecular foundation for early glioma diagnosis, monitoring therapeutic response, and prognostic evaluation [14, 15].

Studies demonstrate that GBM derived exosomes can transverse the BBB and deliver unique molecular cargo into the peripheral circulation, distinct from free circulating miRNA [16]. This establishes GBM derived exosomes as a critical platform for discovering biomarkers to monitor glioma progression. Furthermore, BIGH3, identified within GBM derived exosomes, emerges as a promising prognostic biomarker [17]. Importantly, exosomal BIGH3 expression levels dynamically correlate with therapeutic response to temozolomide (TMZ) in gliomas, highlighting its dual utility for prognosis and treatment monitoring.

Furthermore, titanium dioxide (TiO₂)-based local surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) technology effectively tracks BIGH3 expression levels, providing a powerful platform to monitor TMZ anti-tumor efficacy and evaluate post treatment prognosis [18]. This methodology enables quantitative analysis of glioma derived exosomes and precise identification of the surface marker CD63. Collectively, TiO₂-LSPR offers a high-precision approach for exosomal biomarker detection and characterization, significantly advancing methodological capabilities in the field [19].

Separately, intramedullary astrocytomas, exhibit distinct molecular biomarkers. The most characterized alterations include mutations in TP53, H3F3A, and ATRX [20]. Preliminary evidence suggests these molecular signatures may potentially be detectable within exosomes. however, experimental validation remains necessary to substantiate this hypothesis.

Quantitative PCR analysis of serum-derived exosomes revealed significantly elevated levels of exo-miR-210 in glioma patients compared to healthy controls. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis further indicated exo-miR-210’s potential as a dual biomarker for glioma detection and hypoxia assessment, demonstrating diagnostic, prognostic, and hypoxia-monitoring utility [9]. Separately, in GBM, the most aggressive glioma subtype comprising 50% of cases, a 2021 study identified dysregulated circular RNAs (circRNAs) in plasma exosomes. GBM patients exhibited reduced expression of circSMARCA5 and circHIPK3 [21], while circ0074920, circ0055202, and circ0043722 were significantly upregulated versus controls. Functional validation demonstrated that silencing these three circRNAs suppressed proliferation in U87 GBM cells. These findings nominate specific circRNAs as candidate GBM biomarkers and reveal promising molecular targets for diagnosis and treatment response monitoring [22].

Liquid biopsy, a minimally invasive, cost-effective, and real time capable method for tumor monitoring, is attracting significant attention in cancer diagnostics. Exosomes, extracellular vesicles actively secreted by living cells, are ubiquitous in human biofluids. Owing to this accessibility and their molecular cargo, exosomes constitute a rich source of biomarkers for liquid biopsy applications [23, 24].

sec.title: The role of exosomes in tumor development
sec.p: Exosomes, nanoscale extracellular vesicles actively secreted by cells, critically regulate tumor development. They participate not only in tumor cell growth and proliferation but also facilitate invasion, metastasis, and drug resistance, thereby promoting tumor progression.

sec.title: Exosomes regulate signaling pathways to influence the development of glioma
sec.p: Exosomes encapsulate miRNAs, proteins, and other bioactive molecules whose composition undergoes dynamic alterations during distinct stages of cancer progression [25, 26]. Among these cargo components, exosomal miRNAs function as central regulators in tumor oncogenesis [27–29]. Recent evidence demonstrates that exosomal miRNAs modulate key signaling pathways, directly implicating them in glioma pathogenesis [10]. For instance, exosomal miR-5096 enhances glioma cell invasiveness by directly targeting the K⁺ channel Kir4.1, thereby promoting filopodia formation. Concurrently, miR-5096 increases exosome biogenesis and release, contributing to GBM metastatic dissemination [30].

sec.title: Exosomes regulate the tumor microenvironment
sec.p: During tumor initiation and progression, invasive tumor cells establish a complex tumor microenvironment (TME). This ecosystem comprises immune cells, stromal components, vascular endothelial cells (ECs), and the Extracellular Matrix. Through dynamic interactions, these cellular and structural elements create a functionally diverse niche that critically modulates tumor cell behaviors-including proliferation, invasion, metastasis, and therapeutic response [31].

The TME critically drives glioma progression, serving as a primary regulator of oncogenesis, tumor growth, and therapeutic resistance [32]. Within this ecosystem, glioma derived exosomes particularly those from GBM significantly remodel stromal cell immune functions through their unique molecular cargo. Specifically, GBM exosomes reprogram tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), inducing the release of exosomes laden with immunosuppressive factors and tumor promoting cytokines. This cascade fosters an immunosuppressive niche that accelerates malignant progression [33].

Under hypoxic conditions, exosomal expression of CD44 and CD133 is significantly upregulated. This elevation critically enhances glioma cell migration and promotes endothelial lumen formation, thereby driving tumor invasion and angiogenesis [18]. Separately, glioblastoma stem cell derived exosomes deliver STAT3 signaling molecules that translocate into monocyte cytoplasm. This transfer induces actin cytoskeletal reorganization and promotes monocyte polarization toward the M2 phenotype, facilitate immune evasion and microenvironment remodeling [34].

Exosomes derived from dendritic cells demonstrate distinct biological functions, notably enhancing anti-tumor immune responses. Specifically, DC exosomes activate regulatory T cell (Treg) subsets, thereby augmenting their capacity for tumor recognition and cytotoxicity. This positions DC exosomes as a promising strategy for tumor immunotherapy [31]. Furthermore, exosomes released by lipopolysaccharide-and interferon-γ-stimulated microglia effectively inhibit glioma progression by inducing phenotypic transformation in TAMs [35]. Additionally, Treg derived exosomes mediate immunosuppressive effects on target cells by conveying immunosuppressive cargo [36]. Mechanistically, the immunosuppressive function of Treg exosomes primarily relies on their miRNA content, which inhibits Th1 cell proliferation and cytokine release, thus playing a critical role in immune regulation [37].

sec.title: Exosomes promote angiogenesis
sec.p: Exosomes secreted by U251 human glioma cells are enriched with pro-angiogenic components. These exosomes enhance endothelial cell (EC) angiogenic capacity by promoting EC growth, migration, and lumen formation [38]. Mechanistically, glioma-derived exosomes regulate EC function through modulation of miRNA expression. Specifically, exosomes derived from glioma stem cells induce EC angiogenic potential by upregulating miR-21, pro-angiogenic growth factors, and vascular endothelial growth factor, thereby promoting angiogenesis [39]. Studies show that glioma cells promote angiogenesis and suppress EC apoptosis through exosome-mediated delivery of the long non-coding RNA CCAT2. This mechanism establishes a permissive tumor microenvironment that facilitates progression and invasion [40].

Exosomes serve as critical mediators in the highly complex process of glioma progression. Consequently, comprehensive characterization of their diverse biological functions is indispensable for elucidating glioma pathogenesis and advancing clinical therapeutic strategies.

sec.title: Exosomes as drug delivery vectors for glioma
sec.p: Recent research underscores exosomes as an emerging drug delivery platform(Fig. 11), demonstrating significant multifunctional advantages over conventional delivery systems. Specifically, exosomes efficiently transport diverse molecular cargo-including mRNA, miRNA, and proteins-and achieve precise delivery to target cells. A key attribute is their ability to traverse critical biological barriers, such as the BBB, thereby accessing tissues poorly served by systemic circulation, including densely structured cartilage. Furthermore, exosomes exhibit a low clearance rate, enabling prolonged retention within target tissues and conferring distinct therapeutic benefits. Collectively, these superior properties establish exosomes as a highly promising modality for broad drug delivery applications [41].

sec.title: Exosomes can pass through the blood-brain barrier
sec.p: Despite the application of diverse drugs and therapies, effective treatment of glioma remains challenging. A major obstacle is the BBB, which significantly impedes drug delivery to target sites. As the principal regulatory interface between the CNS and systemic circulation, the BBB functions as both a physical and metabolic barrier, restricting substance exchange between blood and neural tissue. It protects the CNS by excluding neurotoxic plasma components, blood cells, and pathogens, thereby maintaining brain homeostasis and shielding neural tissue from harmful bloodborne substances and microorganisms. Consequently, the BBB critically hinders the efficient delivery of therapeutic agents to gliomas [42, 43].

Consequently, nanomaterial based drug delivery systems represent a promising strategy to overcome the BBB and achieve targeted drug delivery. Among these systems, exosomes have garnered significant research interest as non-viral delivery vectors. Critically, exosomes exhibit innate capacity to cross both the BBB and blood cerebrospinal fluid barrier without triggering immune rejection. This unique property enables efficient delivery of small-molecule therapeutics to gliomas and other brain tumors [44]. Although research into exosome-based brain tumor therapy remains nascent, significant efforts focus on developing these biological carriers and optimizing personalized modulation strategies to enhance drug delivery efficiency [45]. This focus is particularly relevant due to the limitations of traditional nanocarriers, which often exhibit poor tissue compatibility, compromised bioactivity, and inadequate tumor selectivity, thereby diminishing therapeutic efficacy [46].

sec.title: Exosomes have a natural nanoscale size
sec.p: Exosomes, nanoscale extracellular vesicles constitutively released by cells, function as natural carriers for diverse therapeutic cargo including lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids [47]. Their exceptional biological stability derives from low immunogenicity, superior biocompatibility, favorable tissue tolerance, and a protective lipid bilayer membrane. Recent studies demonstrate that exosomal vesicles engineered with transcriptional peptide trans-activator (TAT) and angiopeptide-2 exhibit not only dual-drug loading capacity but also enhanced cellular penetration. Notably, these functionalized exosomes effectively traverse the BBB and achieve precise targeting of glioma lesions [48]. Consequently, exosomes hold significant therapeutic promise as versatile platforms: drug delivery vehicles, cancer vaccine scaffolds, and biomarkers for diagnosis, therapy monitoring, and prognosis. These applications constitute major research frontiers attracting significant investigation [49, 50].

sec.title: Exosomes possess targeting ability
sec.p: Exosomes function as precision delivery vehicles through surface functionalization with targeting ligands such as proteins, peptides, or aptamers [51]. Transmembrane proteins-including integrins, tetraspanins, and intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1)-embedded within the exosomal membrane mediate cell- and tissue-specific targeting. Strategic modification of these molecular components significantly enhances delivery specificity, thereby optimizing exosomal efficacy in biomedical applications [52]. Comparative studies demonstrate that exosome-encapsulated doxorubicin (DOX) achieves 2.3-fold higher cellular uptake rates and 1.8-fold greater intracellular accumulation versus free DOX and liposomal-DOX across multiple cell lines [53]. This evidence establishes exosomes as superior drug carriers with enhanced membrane permeability and accumulation kinetics. Notably, brain endothelial cell derived exosomes loaded with DOX nanoparticles enable tumor specific drug delivery with precise spatial localization. Subsequent drug aggregation within tumor microenvironments induces dual cytotoxic mechanisms: direct tumor cell apoptosis and immunogenic cell death (ICD). The ICD cascade promotes dendritic cell maturation and cytotoxic lymphocyte infiltration/activation, eliciting potent anti-tumor immunity in GBM murine models [54]. These findings advance novel immunotherapeutic strategies for oncological applications.

Wang et al. engineered a DOX delivery platform using neutrophil derived exosomes (NEs-Exos). Experimental data demonstrate that NEs-Exos efficiently traverse the BBB and exhibit chemotactic responsiveness to inflammatory stimuli within gliomas, enabling precise targeting of tumor-associated inflammatory niches [55]. Furthermore, surface functionalization of exosomes with tissue specific ligands through genetic engineering or biochemical conjugation significantly enhances targeting precision.

Complementary research by Zhu et al. revealed that angiopep-2 (ANG) binds with high affinity to low density lipoprotein receptorrelated protein-1, a receptor overexpressed on BBB endothelial cells and glioma cells. Dual modification of exosomes with TAT peptide and ANG synergistically enhanced DOX penetration into tumor parenchyma, resulting in significantly improved therapeutic outcomes in glioma models [48].

sec.title: Challenges faced by the application of exosomes and prediction of future research directions
sec.p: The advancement of exosomes as drug delivery platforms represents a major frontier in biomedical research. Currently, ultracentrifugation (UC) remains the predominant isolation method, along with techniques such as ultrafiltration, size-exclusion chromatography (SEC), density gradient centrifugation, immunoaffinity capture, polymer precipitation, and microfluidic approaches. While UC is established as the reference standard owing to its high purity, this method exhibits significant limitations, including low recovery rates, substantial sample loss during processing, and potential alterations to exosome structural and functional integrity. Consequently, developing efficient, minimally disruptive isolation techniques has become imperative to fulfill the requirements of both fundamental research and clinical translation [56].

The preparation of therapeutic grade exosomes necessitates careful evaluation of critical parameters including processing time, cost efficiency, yield optimization, and sample specific variables. Consequently, establishing separation and purification protocols that simultaneously ensure high purity, efficiency, and simplicity represents a critical prerequisite for the clinical translation of exosome based drug delivery systems. Methodological optimization remains essential to maximize both exosome yield and biological integrity, thereby ensuring therapeutic efficacy and safety profiles.

Exosomal drug loading is a key research focus, primarily categorized into two strategies: endogenous loading during natural biogenesis and exogenous loading via external manipulation. Therapeutic cargo including proteins, pharmaceuticals, and small nucleic acids exhibits variable encapsulation efficiency dependent on exosome cellular origin. While endogenous loading aligns with physiological biosynthesis pathways, its technical complexity and time intensive nature present significant limitations.

To overcome these constraints, Yang et al. pioneered cell nanoporation technology [57]. This innovative approach achieves 50-fold higher exosome yields and 10³-fold greater mRNA transcription efficiency versus conventional electroporation, resulting in significantly enhanced therapeutic efficacy in glioma models. Comparatively, exogenous loading methods offer superior controllability in encapsulation efficiency and payload capacity. Collectively, these methodological advances establish new paradigms for exosome-based drug delivery systems [58].

To date, numerous exogenous loading techniques-including freeze-thaw cycles, extrusion, incubation, electroporation, sonication, and permeabilization methods-have been developed for encapsulating therapeutic agents into exosomes [59]. This versatility enables the tailoring of drug loading approaches to specific delivery requirements. Consequently, the advancement of efficient exosomal drug loading technologies and their subsequent translation into scalable production and clinical application represent a critical focus and emerging research frontier within the field of exosome therapeutics.

Exosomes have garnered substantial interest in disease biology research, with their potential applications in diagnosis, prognosis, and therapy continuing to expand. In glioma therapeutics, exosomes are actively investigated both as inherent therapeutics and engineered drug delivery systems. Despite extensive preclinical research, clinical translation of exosome based therapies faces critical biological and technical challenges, necessitating innovative strategies and further mechanistic investigation [60].

sec.title: Advantages and limitations
sec.p: This study employed bibliometric analysis, utilizing VOS and CiteSpace, to systematically map the current research landscape and identify key research foci regarding exosomes in glioma. Bibliometrics serves as a robust scientometric approach, providing an objective and visualized overview of the developmental trajectory and emerging trends within a specific research domain. Through this analysis, we delineate the current state of exosome research in glioma, enabling the identification of prominent research directions, influential publications, and leading journals within this field.

However, this study has several limitations that warrant consideration. First, concerning data sources, the analysis was restricted to literature retrieved from the WOSCC. The exclusion of other major databases, such as PubMed and Scopus, may have resulted in an incomplete literature corpus. Consequently, this could affect the comprehensiveness of the analysis and carry the risk of omitting significant research directions and emerging topics. Second, regarding language inclusion, only English-language publications were incorporated. This exclusion of non-English literature potentially limits the scope of the findings and may overlook important contributions from non-English-speaking regions.

sec.title: Conclusion
sec.p: Utilizing VOS and CiteSpace for bibliometric analysis, this study conducted an in-depth investigation of exosome-related literature in glioma research, presenting findings through visualizations. The analysis delineated the developmental trajectory of the field, identified current research hotspots, and suggested potential future research directions. Publication output in this domain has exhibited a steady increase since 2019, indicating growing global research interest in exosomes, with substantial contributions originating from China. Recent research foci have centered on key areas including tumor microenvironment associated signaling pathways, temozolomide resistance, and exosome-mediated drug delivery. Future investigations are likely to prioritize the development of exosomes as targeted delivery systems for glioma therapeutics. Further research is imperative to fully elucidate the therapeutic potential of exosomes in glioma. Bibliometric analysis proves valuable for identifying emerging trends and guiding research objectives, thereby facilitating advancements in glioma treatment strategies.
